title: AFTERIMAGE / COMPASS SIGNALS
notice: BC AI Compass originally verified these organization sources on their stated source dates. This is a dated subset, not a current job feed or partnership assertion. Geographic markers are source-stated locations or municipal centroids; most are NOT office locations.

source.name: BC AI Compass by Martin Montero
source.attribution: BC AI Compass (bc-aicompass.ca), dataset by Martin Montero, CC BY 4.0
source.changes: Filtered to Metro Vancouver and Province-wide verified organizations, removed people and contact fields; kept source URLs/dates/coordinates/precision; grouped identical points rather than inventing office locations. Added a four-record editorial ID/name crosswalk to matching Observatory archive entries (same-entity references, NOT partnership claims).
source.affiliate_notice: AFTERIMAGE is independently made; this import does not claim BC AI Compass or listed organizations endorse AFTERIMAGE.

organizations.name: AbCellera Biologics
organizations.description: Vancouver biotechnology company that describes itself as integrating biology, computation and engineering to develop antibody-based medicines, with in-house clinical manufacturing in Vancouver. Its own pages do not use the term AI; it is listed here as part of the province’s computational life-sciences base, not on a claim it makes about itself.

organizations.name: AI and Technology-Enhanced Emergency Care Collaboration Centre (AiTECCC)
organizations.description: Cluster bringing health leaders and AI experts together to co-design AI-powered healthcare solutions.

organizations.name: AI Creativity + Design
organizations.description: A BC + AI special-interest group its own page describes as a forming group, with first-session cadence not confirmed and no host names confirmed publicly yet.

organizations.name: AI Ethical Futures Lab
organizations.description: BC + AI's civic policy lab, described on its own page as not a panel but a working room for people who want AI's possibilities without surrendering agency, accountability, or public voice. Meets monthly at Parker Street Studios.

organizations.name: AIM Lab — Artificial Intelligence in Medicine Lab
organizations.description: Develops AI and machine-learning methods for cancer diagnosis and healthcare delivery, including image analysis that helps clinicians examine tissue and identify cancerous cells.

organizations.name: AMLTN — Advanced Machine Learning Training Network
organizations.description: Builds a research training programme in machine learning with opportunities beyond traditional computer science education, connecting students to researchers globally.

organizations.name: Artificial Intelligence Methods for Scientific Impact (AIM-SI)
organizations.description: Interdisciplinary cluster within CAIDA, established to expand UBC’s teaching and research capacity in artificial intelligence.

organizations.name: Aspect Biosystems
organizations.description: Vancouver bioprinting company developing therapeutic programs from its own bioprinting platform. Its contact page does not describe AI or machine-learning work; the AI-enabled characterisation comes from secondary research and is not asserted here.

organizations.name: BC + AI Ecosystem Association
organizations.description: Non-profit association describing itself as 300+ paying members building British Columbia’s AI industry, running regional chapters, certifications, the AI Builders Fellowship and the Futureproof Festival. No founding year is published here: the association’s own About page and press kit give different years, and picking one would be choosing rather than sourcing. BC AI Compass is a BC + AI Ecosystem Association project, so this is the one record in the directory published by its own commissioning organization.

organizations.name: BC + AI Film Club
organizations.description: BC + AI's creative special-interest group, described on its own page as a monthly meetup for people making films with AI.

organizations.name: BC Cancer
organizations.description: Named as a participating investigator organization in a British Columbia ovarian cancer project using AI to identify factors tied to long-term survival.

organizations.name: BC Hydro
organizations.description: Provincial Crown utility. Runs the competitive selection process, opened 30 January 2026 under Bill 31, that allocates electricity to AI and data-centre projects — up to 400 MW over the first two years, evaluated on price and on economic, community, data sovereignty and environmental benefits.

organizations.name: BC Tech Association
organizations.location: Vancouver — 210-1401 West 8th Avenue (mailing address; fully virtual team)
organizations.description: British Columbia’s cross-sector technology industry association, running member programmes, accelerators, talent and immigration initiatives and advocacy. Its AI-specific programming includes a vertical accelerator aimed at AI companies.

organizations.name: BCNET
organizations.description: Not-for-profit shared-services organization for British Columbia’s higher-education and research institutions. Reported as the network through which the Thompson Rivers University AI facility provides training and inference compute to students and faculty.

organizations.name: CAIDA — UBC Centre for Artificial Intelligence Decision-making and Action
organizations.location: Vancouver — 289-2366 Main Mall, ICICS Building, UBC Vancouver
organizations.description: Described by UBC as the university’s research hub for artificial intelligence, spanning many departments and working on theoretical and applied AI for decision-making and action. Sits within UBC’s Institute for Computing, Information and Cognitive Systems.

organizations.name: City of Vancouver
organizations.description: Named in the TELUS release as a partner in the sovereign AI factory cluster being developed in Vancouver. Listed here for that stated role.

organizations.name: Computational Design Lab
organizations.description: Explores how design transforms through computation, creating ideas, interfaces, algorithms and systems for change.

organizations.name: Computational Neuroscience Research Lab
organizations.description: Investigates brain plasticity and neuro-training to develop digital health solutions.

organizations.name: Creative Energy
organizations.description: Named in the TELUS release as a partner in the Vancouver sovereign AI factory cluster, whose design is described as using every electron twice.

organizations.name: Dapper Labs
organizations.description: Vancouver-based consumer blockchain company with hubs in Los Angeles, New York and Charlotte. Its careers page describes AI tooling as standard across the company.

organizations.name: Data & Dialogue Lab
organizations.description: Research at the intersection of information visualization, human-computer interaction and social psychology.

organizations.name: Data Science and Health (DASH)
organizations.description: Cluster building systems to link health research data in British Columbia, to improve diagnosis, treatment and disease prevention.

organizations.name: DigiBC
organizations.description: Registered non-profit industry association for British Columbia’s creative technology sector — video games, animation, visual effects, XR and virtual production — working on advocacy, talent pipeline, equity and community programming. Founded in 1997 as New Media BC and renamed in January 2009, so New Media BC is a former name of this organization rather than a separate one.

organizations.name: DIGITAL
organizations.description: One of Canada’s Global Innovation Clusters, formerly and still widely known as the Digital Technology Supercluster. Co-invests federal and industry money in applied technology projects, and runs a dedicated artificial intelligence programme stream.

organizations.name: Digital Democracies Institute
organizations.description: SFU institute listed as using AI to create innovations in digital democracy and related fields.

organizations.name: Ed + AI: Education Meetup
organizations.description: A BC + AI education community giving educators, youth, families and builders a practical place to compare what is happening in classrooms and community learning spaces. Its own page describes a consent-first learning circle with Ethọ́s Lab and names Ethọ́s Lab as the public partner.

organizations.name: Ethọ́s Lab
organizations.description: Youth STEAM academy in Vancouver running afterschool project-based programs and in-school activations for youth in Grades 5–12, grounding its approach in the African philosophy of Ubuntu.

organizations.name: First Nations Technology Council
organizations.description: Indigenous-led non-profit mandated by the First Nations Leadership Council to advance digital literacy, connectivity and technology strategy for all 204 First Nations in British Columbia. Its AI work includes the course "Pathways to AI: An Introduction for Indigenous People and Organizations" and the report "First Nations Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence".

organizations.name: General Fusion
organizations.description: Fusion energy company headquartered in Richmond. Listed as part of British Columbia’s advanced-computing and deep-tech base; its contact page does not describe AI or machine-learning work, and no such claim is made here.

organizations.name: Graphical AI
organizations.description: Cluster bridging mathematics and computer science to uncover cause-and-effect relationships in public health research.

organizations.name: Graphics, Usability and Visualization (GrUVI) Group
organizations.description: Addresses computer graphics, user experience design and data visualization.

organizations.name: Human-AI Interaction @ UBC (HAI)
organizations.description: Works at the intersection of AI, human-computer interaction and cognitive science on ethical AI systems people can trust, with an emphasis on visualization and decision-support interfaces.

organizations.name: Innovate BC
organizations.location: Vancouver — Four Bentall Centre, 1055 Dunsmuir Street, Suite 810
organizations.description: Provincial Crown agency supporting technology and innovation across British Columbia through hiring grants, mentorship, research grants, pilot funding and innovation challenges, and advising government on technology policy. Programmes named on its site include BC Fast Pilot, Integrated Marketplace, Ignite, Accelerate IP, ScaleUp and the Venture Acceleration Program.

organizations.name: Institute for Neuroscience and Neurotechnology (INN)
organizations.description: SFU institute applying AI to neuroscience research and neurotechnology development.

organizations.name: Integrated Science Lab
organizations.description: Bridges science and technology across decision intelligence, visual analytics, design and behavioural science.

organizations.name: International Cybercrime Research Centre (ICRC)
organizations.description: SFU centre listed as leveraging AI for cybercrime investigation and analysis.

organizations.name: iViz Lab
organizations.description: Focused on AI-based computational models of human characteristics such as expression, emotion, behaviour, empathy and creativity.

organizations.name: Jane Software
organizations.description: Practice-management software for health and wellness clinics, headquartered in North Vancouver, with an AI Scribe feature named under its charting and care tools.

organizations.name: Learning Analytics Lab
organizations.description: Uses data science and machine learning to develop theories supporting educational technologies.

organizations.name: Life Sciences & AI
organizations.description: A BC + AI domain community for life sciences people, covering drug discovery, clinical care, health data, capital and policy. Its own page describes a four-part monthly series running September to December 2026, one running conversation with a different question on each date.

organizations.name: Metacreation Lab for Creative AI
organizations.description: Develops generative systems and algorithms for creative tasks, from human-driven co-creation tools to autonomous creative agents.

organizations.name: MILD — Mathematics of Information, Learning and Data
organizations.description: Cross-departmental group focused on the rigorous mathematics underlying machine learning and data science, including privacy, algorithm design and learning theory.

organizations.name: Mind, AI and Consciousness (MAC)
organizations.description: A BC + AI research community running Deep Dives roughly monthly, alongside Labs, Takeovers and Socials through the year. Thirteen Deep Dives are recorded as completed on its own page.

organizations.name: MineSense Technologies
organizations.description: Sensor and ore-sorting company for mining, with global headquarters in Vancouver. Its about page describes data solutions and a client data portal; it does not name AI, and none is asserted here.

organizations.name: Ministry of Energy and Climate Solutions
organizations.description: Provincial ministry that, with BC Hydro, established the competitive clean-power process for AI and data centres under Bill 31, the Energy Statutes Amendment Act.

organizations.name: MUSIC — Multi-Scale Multi-Modal Image and Omics Computing for Health
organizations.description: NSERC CREATE training programme integrating AI and machine-learning skills with imaging and omics biological data.

organizations.name: New Ventures BC
organizations.description: Supports BC technology startups with mentorship, funding and an annual competition, and runs the Discovery Foundation AI Business Accelerator, which helps BC companies move beyond experimentation with workshops, mentorship and an AI implementation plan.

organizations.name: Niricson
organizations.description: Infrastructure condition assessment for dams, bridges and airfields. Its AUTOSPEX product uses AI and machine learning to establish a digital asset baseline and to detect cracks, delamination, thermal anomalies and spalling.

organizations.name: Novarc Technologies
organizations.description: Builds autonomous welding robots and an AI-powered robotic vision system, NovAI, that adds vision and cognition to articulated robotic and mechanized welders.

organizations.name: Optimization, Learning, Control — UBC Electrical & Computer Engineering
organizations.description: One of six ECE research areas, formulating and solving fundamental problems in learning systems with applications including robotics and transportation.

organizations.name: OVCARE — B.C.’s Ovarian Cancer Research Program
organizations.description: British Columbia ovarian cancer research programme with a director of AI research, using state-of-the-art AI to help predict survival and guide treatment selection.

organizations.name: PacifiCan
organizations.description: Pacific Economic Development Canada, the federal development agency for British Columbia. Administers the Regional Artificial Intelligence Initiative, which funds organizations commercializing or adopting AI in BC — up to $3M per project for businesses and $5M for not-for-profits.

organizations.name: PLAI — Pacific Laboratory for Artificial Intelligence
organizations.description: Develops production-quality open-source software for neuroscience, image recognition and robotics.

organizations.name: Project ADA
organizations.description: Autonomous discovery platform for thin-film materials, using self-driving laboratories and machine learning to accelerate discovery of clean-energy materials.

organizations.name: Quantum Algorithms Institute
organizations.description: Non-profit described on its own site as "dedicated to advancing the growth, adoption, and strategic development of quantum technologies in British Columbia", through quantum literacy in business, training, and pilot projects applying quantum methods. Listed by SFU as developing quantum computing algorithms and AI applications. No physical address is published on its site, so this record carries no coordinates.

organizations.name: Robots with Social Intelligence and Empathy (ROSIE) Lab
organizations.description: Focuses on developing robots with social and empathetic capabilities.

organizations.name: Sanctuary AI
organizations.description: Legally Sanctuary Cognitive Systems Corporation. Deploys what it calls Physical AI on robotic hardware to automate complex industrial tasks, with work spanning AI-driven dexterous manipulation, reinforcement learning for robotics and sim-to-real transfer.

organizations.name: Science and Technology for Aging Research Institute
organizations.description: SFU institute using AI to address challenges in aging populations and senior care.

organizations.name: SFU Big Data Hub
organizations.description: SFU hub that publishes and coordinates the university’s data-intensive and artificial intelligence research activity.

organizations.name: SFU School of Computing Science
organizations.description: Publishes six research areas including artificial intelligence, whose stated scope is machine learning, computer vision, natural language processing, knowledge representation and reasoning, constraint optimization, and robotics.

organizations.name: Simon Fraser University
organizations.description: Publishes an AI research portfolio spanning six institutes and, separately, more than twenty named labs and groups in Computing Science and Interactive Arts & Technology.

organizations.name: Smart Retention
organizations.description: Interdisciplinary cluster addressing nursing workforce retention in Canada using AI and human-centred design.

organizations.name: TELUS
organizations.description: Operator of the proposed sovereign AI factory cluster in British Columbia — Kamloops plus two Vancouver sites — built on an initial 85 MW of clean power secured from BC Hydro. TELUS projects the cluster scaling to over 60,000 GPUs and 150 MW by 2032, roughly $9B in economic value to BC and 1,000+ construction jobs. Those are company projections, not delivered results.

organizations.name: TELUS 150 West Georgia AI Factory
organizations.description: Third and largest-dated facility in the TELUS sovereign AI factory cluster, developed with Westbank and Allied Properties REIT. TELUS states a 2029 start. Permitting is also subject to confirmation of compliance with British Columbia’s new data-centre regulatory framework, so this site is proposed, not approved.

organizations.name: TELUS M3 AI Factory
organizations.description: Proposed AI factory at the former Hootsuite building in Vancouver’s Mount Pleasant, developed with Westbank. TELUS states an end-of-2026 opening scaling through 2028 — but the rezoning remains unresolved: on 21 July 2026 Vancouver City Council reversed its own 14 July decision to send it to a public hearing, deferring the matter past the municipal election. This site is proposed, not approved.

organizations.name: Terramera
organizations.description: Agricultural technology company combining its Actigate technology with data science and AI. Its site states that machine learning engines and monitoring tools continuously generate insights to improve formulation efficacy and plant health.

organizations.name: The University of British Columbia
organizations.description: Publishes a university-wide AI research portfolio spanning institutes, networks and research-excellence clusters across 27 departments.

organizations.name: Trulioo
organizations.description: Identity verification and business-verification platform headquartered in Vancouver, naming agentic AI for resolving beneficial owners inside its know-your-business workflow.

organizations.name: TrustML
organizations.description: Cluster working on trustworthy machine-learning systems that are reliable, secure, explainable and ethical.

organizations.name: UBC AI and Health Network
organizations.description: Initiative combining UBC’s strengths in AI, health-systems research and biomedical innovation, aimed at transforming patient care and accelerating health-system innovation in BC.

organizations.name: UBC Artificial Intelligence Research Group
organizations.description: Computer Science research group focused on decision-making systems designed to cooperate with human decision-makers, including in areas such as privacy.

organizations.name: UBC Computer Vision Lab (CVL)
organizations.description: Develops algorithms for image understanding, video analysis, 3D vision, and applications of generative models in computer vision.

organizations.name: UBC Data Management and Mining Lab (DMM)
organizations.description: Focuses on how to manage or mine data, relational or otherwise.

organizations.name: UBC Data Science Institute
organizations.description: Faculty-wide institute that incubates research, innovation and training in data-intensive science and supplies approaches, tools and expertise for working with large data.

organizations.name: UBC Department of Computer Science
organizations.description: Publishes twenty named research groups, including dedicated groups for artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, natural language processing and data mining.

organizations.name: UBC Information Visualization Group (InfoVis)
organizations.description: Creates visual representations that let people explore and understand large information datasets.

organizations.name: UBC Machine Learning Group
organizations.description: Machine learning research spanning computer science, statistics, mathematics and applied sciences.

organizations.name: UBC Natural Language Processing Group
organizations.description: Research on core natural language processing problems, computational linguistics, text mining, machine learning and visual text analytics.

organizations.name: UBC School of Biomedical Engineering
organizations.description: Home of faculty leading AI research in cancer pathology, including the director of AI research for British Columbia’s ovarian cancer research programme.

organizations.name: UBC Security and Privacy Group
organizations.description: Works on systems security, cloud security, privacy, machine learning and software engineering.

organizations.name: UBC Sensorimotor Systems Lab (SSL)
organizations.description: Researches human movement through computer graphics, scientific computing, robotics and biomechanics.

organizations.name: Vancouver AI
organizations.location: Vancouver — H.R. MacMillan Space Centre, 1100 Chestnut St
organizations.description: BC + AI's flagship regional room, labelled on the communities index as the original room where the ecosystem gathers in person before the work fans out across the province. Meets monthly at the H.R. MacMillan Space Centre.

organizations.name: Vancouver Coastal Health Research Institute
organizations.description: Health research institute of Vancouver Coastal Health and a UBC health partner, with Digital Health and Artificial Intelligence as a named research focus area.

organizations.name: Vancouver Institute for Visual Analytics (VIVA)
organizations.description: Institute focused on visual analytics, using AI for data visualization and interpretation.

organizations.name: Variational AI
organizations.description: Uses generative AI to design novel, synthesizable small molecules optimized across potency, selectivity, ADMET and synthetic feasibility for early-stage drug discovery.

organizations.name: VCH-VCHRI AI Hub
organizations.description: Support service listed by Vancouver Coastal Health Research Institute for AI work across the health authority and institute.

organizations.name: Visier
organizations.description: People-analytics and workforce-planning company headquartered in Vancouver, stating 600 employees across seven offices. Part of the province’s applied-analytics base.

organizations.name: Visual & Interactive Computing Institute (VINCI)
organizations.description: Established at SFU in 2023, combining Computing Science and the School of Interactive Arts & Technology to lead innovation in visual computing, artificial intelligence and human-computer interaction.

organizations.name: Westbank
organizations.description: Named in the TELUS release as the development partner for the two new Vancouver AI factory facilities. Listed here for that stated role; no separate AI activity was verified.

organizations.name: Zymeworks
organizations.description: Biotherapeutics company with its head office in Vancouver. Its contact page does not describe AI or machine-learning work, and none is asserted here.
